top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Étape du Dales. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 106 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Étape du Dales' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
10,500ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
99ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Étape du Dales, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 106, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Étape du Dales. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Étape du Dales. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 106 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
10,500ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 10,500ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Étape du Dales’s 106 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Étape du Dales includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at Étape du Dales demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride mixed terrain at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and VO2max to prepare you for 106 miles of mixed terrain in Settle, North Yorkshire, England.
